messages:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing a jump in GPU attach failures in us-west2-b. Inference pods on g4/g5 pools get 'nvlink timeout' and p2p latency spikes. Started ~09:12 UTC. Logs below.

maria: ```
kubectl logs inference-abc-57 --since=5m
E: gpu_attach timeout after 30s
E: topology query failed: p2p latency 120ms
```

lee: I can repro on node gpu-usw2b-34 — NIC counters show packet drops on mellanox port 2.

aj: Recommend marking affected nodes unschedulable and moving pods. Which ASG to scale? we should avoid mass preemptions.

ops-janet: Scaling reserved pool in us-west2-c and -a now: increasing inference-reserved-asg by +12. Command: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name inference-reserved-usw2c --desired-capacity 28`

deploy-bot: Autoscaler: set-desired-capacity(inference-reserved-usw2c)=28 -> scaling started, est warmup 6m

lee: I'll cordon nodes with label zone=us-west2b,gpu-type=gpu-a100 and migrate user pods. Running:
`kubectl cordon gpu-usw2b-* && kubectl drain gpu-usw2b-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`

maria: Also temporarily adjust routing weights: nginx upstream inference -> decrease weight for us-west2b backends by 60%.

sre-bot: Routing update queued: shift 60% of us-west2b traffic -> other AZs. Canary 20% now.

lee: Canary applied (20%), monitoring metrics (99th latency, attach errors). If stable for 5m, continue. :eyes:

maria: Cost/priority note: for critical paths we'll prefer on-demand instances in reserve pools to avoid spot churn — ops-janet ok to force on-demand for the temporarily scaled hosts?

ops-janet: Confirmed, new instances will be on-demand for priority pools for the duration. Cost impact estimated ~+$0.08/sess/min for hot routes.

aj: Post-action: created incident ticket INC-19712 and linked runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/zone-net-flap

maria: Status: 4/18 nodes still showing p2p errors, 12 new reserve instances booting in usw2c/ausa, traffic shifted ~45% away from us-west2b. Continuing to monitor.

lee: Will keep checking NIC counters and open support case with cloud vendor if packet drops persist.

maria: Thanks — next update in 10m unless situation changes. :thumbsup:
